page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.2xlarge is an accelerated virtual instance within the Compute Optimized with GPU family. Running on KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The host architecture provides 33 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES acceleration, and 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural element is the integration of an NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM for hardware-accelerated processing. Networking is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no local disk storage is included.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the host CPU subsystem exhibits moderate to lower-tier performance across synthetic suites. In Geekbench, the instance recorded a single-core score of 604.0 and a multi-core score of 2324.0, while PassMark yielded a CPU score of 6136.75. Stress-ng returned 1108.28 in single-core and 5895.65 in multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth measurements show steady write speeds at 35.65 GB/sec, alongside an uncached read throughput of 39.02 GB/sec. Application tests registered 5.66 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 4.71 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on the reliance on the attached Volta V100 GPU rather than general CPU horsepower. Because advanced instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are not available to the guest OS, raw host-side compute tasks underperform relative to modern processor tiers. The absence of integrated local storage means data pipelines rely entirely on remote network-attached disks, bounded by the 2 Gbps network baseline. Cost efficiency is shaped by the presence of dedicated GPU acceleration; while raw host compute efficiency is lower, value is realized when application routines effectively leverage the NVIDIA V100 VRAM and parallel compute pipeline.

Appropriate deployment scenarios include deep learning model training, AI inference within the 16 GB VRAM budget, scientific simulations, video rendering, and GPU-accelerated graphics workloads. It is suboptimal for pure CPU-intensive batch jobs or high-throughput storage processing due to the modest CPU benchmarks, lack of advanced vector extensions, and reliance on network storage.
